newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico magnate cleared of tax evasion charges.
newsitem.headline: Mexico magnate cleared of tax evasion charges.

text.p: A judge cleared business magnate Carlos Peralta Quintero Monday of tax evasion charges, less than two months after Mexican authorities had issued a warrant for his arrest.
The Attorney General's office (PGR) said in a statement that it would appeal the judge's decision because of what it termed "trial irregularities".
Peralta, who belongs to one of Mexico's wealthiest families, was accused of illegally evading $6 million in undeclared taxes between 1992 and 1995.

The magnate, whose family owns the Iusa holding company clustering electrical equipment and telecommunications interests, denied guilt and said he had already paid the money before the arrest warrant was issued.
The PGR claimed that the judge's acquittal "contradicted his own resolutions on the same penal case".

Peralta, the former president of Grupo Iusacell, shot into the limelight after admitting having made a $50 million loan without any documentation to Raul Salinas, the jailed brother of former president Carlos Salinas.

Bell Atlantic, the minority partner in Iusacell, subsequently replaced Peralta as president of the telecommunications firm and took management control but the Peralta family retained its shareholding in Iusacell.
